text:
The Maple Leafs are in a slump, and John Tavares is one of the voices trying to pull them out of it. TSN's headline on Nov. 22: "Tavares agrees with Matthews that leadership group needs to guide Leafs out of slump." Toronto has won once in his last ten games.

His own numbers are mixed. He has 4 goals and 10 points in 16 games, 5 on the power play, and scored in back-to-back games against Chicago and Los Angeles. But at five on five the Leafs have been crushed with him on the ice: 37.4% of the expected goals (chance quality), 11 points worse than without him. Some of that is bad luck too: Toronto has scored 5.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, and his 2.18 points per 60 sit just under our talent range.

He's 36, a first overall pick with 1,185 career points before this season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still had him at 98th percentile for chances from in front of the net last season. He missed time between Oct. 15 and Nov. 7. The finishing should come back. The five-on-five numbers are the real worry.
headline: Tavares in a Leafs slump
